views.settings: $r_s = 1$, the unit of every length, and $q = 2\,r_s$.
stops: Inside the horizon, $r < r_s$, $g_{rr} < 0$: $r$ is a time there, and a slice of constant $t$ is not a moment of space.
caption: The equatorial plane ($\theta = \pi/2$) of a Kaluza-Klein black hole of one charge ($q = 2\,r_s$) at one moment of $t$, in the Einstein metric of four dimensions, drawn as a surface in flat space with every distance along it the metric distance. On it the metric is $\sqrt{r(r + q - r_s)}\,(dr^2/(r - r_s) + r\,d\phi^2)$, so the circle at $r$ has the circumference $2\pi(r^3(r + q - r_s))^{1/4}$, longer than $2\pi r$.

The slice passes through the bifurcation sphere $r = r_s$, its smallest circle, of radius $(q\,r_s^3)^{1/4} = 1.19\,r_s$, and runs on into a second exterior, the same surface turned over. At $q = r_s$ the surface is Flamm's paraboloid. The magnetic hole with $p = 2\,r_s$ has the same surface.

views.settings: $r_s = 1$, the unit of every length, $q = 2\,r_s$, and a circle of length $L = 2\pi r_s$, on the surface of $r$ and $y$ ($\theta = 0$).
stops: Inside the horizon, $r < r_s$, $g_{rr} < 0$: $r$ is a time there, and a slice of constant $t$ is not a moment of space.
caption: The surface of $r$ and $y$ ($\theta = 0$) of the electrically charged hole ($q = 2\,r_s$) at one moment of $t$, drawn as a surface in flat space with every distance along it the metric distance. On it the metric is $dr^2/(1 - r_s/r) + (1 + (q - r_s)/r)\,dy^2$, so the circle of the fifth dimension at $r$ has circumference $L\sqrt{1 + (q - r_s)/r}$. Far from the hole the surface is a cylinder, the small circle Klein gave every point of space, drawn with $L = 2\pi r_s$.

Toward the hole the circle grows, and it is widest on the horizon $r = r_s$, where its circumference is $L\sqrt{q/r_s}$. The slice passes through the horizon into a second exterior, the same surface turned over. At $q = r_s$ the hole has no charge and the surface is a cylinder.

views.label: The fifth dimension, magnetic charge

start.text: the horizon $r = r_s$, the narrowest circle, where the other exterior begins

legend: the surface $\theta = 0$ at $t = 0$, which $r > r_s$ and $y$ cover
the same radii on the other exterior

views.settings: $r_s = 1$, the unit of every length, and $p = 2\,r_s$, on the surface of $r$ and $y$ ($\theta = 0$).
stops: Inside the horizon, $r < r_s$, $g_{rr} < 0$: $r$ is a time there, and a slice of constant $t$ is not a moment of space.
caption: The surface of $r$ and $y$ on the half axis $\theta = 0$ of the magnetically charged hole ($p = 2\,r_s$) at one moment of $t$, drawn as a surface in flat space with every distance along it the metric distance. On it the metric is $(1 + (p - r_s)/r)\,dr^2/(1 - r_s/r) + dy^2/(1 + (p - r_s)/r)$, so the circle of the fifth dimension at $r$ has circumference $4\pi\sqrt{p(p - r_s)}\sqrt{r/(r + p - r_s)}$. Far from the hole the surface is a cylinder of radius $2\sqrt{p(p - r_s)}$.

Toward the hole the circle shrinks, and on the horizon $r = r_s$ its radius is $2\sqrt{r_s(p - r_s)}$, the narrowest circle of the slice, which runs on into a second exterior, the same surface turned over. Inside the horizon the circle goes on shrinking and closes at the singularity $r = 0$. At $r_s = 0$ there is no horizon and the surface is the cigar of the Kaluza-Klein monopole, closed smoothly at the nut.
